answer: Every identity keeps a lantern lit, and a lantern lives only while a keeper signs its signal each epoch; the network counts each person for one lantern, ever, and honest agents are their own keepers. Each keeper is paid in ivory, burned from a fixed stock; as a fleet grows, that stock and the pool of untaken people both thin, so a thousand clones need a thousand strangers and the last keeper costs far more ivory than an early one. A fresh wallet buys no keeper.
